expectations.evidence: Verified by reading fixed.kql (auto-grade agrees): `| project Timestamp, ReportId, DeviceId, ...` then `summarize (Timestamp, ReportId) = arg_min(Timestamp, ReportId) ... by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountSid` and `project-reorder Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ... ReportId` keep all three. No `join` anywhere (0 joins, so kind= clause vacuous). Three make_set calls, all capped: `make_set(Tool, MaxContextItems)`, `make_set(ProcessCommandLine, MaxContextItems)`, `make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, MaxContextItems)` with `let MaxContextItems = 20`. No make_list.

claims.claim: fixed.kql is plausibly valid Advanced Hunting KQL (balanced delimiters, real DeviceProcessEvents columns, no obvious syntax errors)
claims.evidence: Comment-stripped delimiter count: 37/37 parens, 3/3 brackets, quotes balanced. All referenced columns exist on DeviceProcessEvents (ActionType, ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName, FileName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, Timestamp, ReportId, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessAccountSid/Domain/Name, InitiatingProcessFileName/CommandLine). `(Timestamp, ReportId) = arg_min(...)`, `in~ (dynamic)`, `replace_string`, `take_any`, `project-reorder` are all valid. One residual: the empty-fence `has_any (ExcludedParentFolders)` with `dynamic([])` relies on has_any over an empty array evaluating false (standard behaviour, but not executable here). Minor: two unused `let query_frequency/query_period` declarations are harmless in AH.

claims.claim: fixed.kql would still fire on a single `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` execution
claims.evidence: Traced: ActionType ProcessCreated -> FileName/OriginalFileName in~ TargetBinaries -> fences empty -> Tool = "vssadmin.exe", Canon contains "delete" and "shadows" -> summarize per DeviceId/account -> EventCount 1 >= MinEvents (let MinEvents = 1). Fires. Also matches without `.exe`, with reordered flags, and with quoted/caret-obfuscated args.

claims.claim: review.md says lint on the original gave '1 error, 7 warnings' and the fix is '--strict clean'
claims.evidence: Fixed query lints clean (0/0). Original-lint count not re-run but consistent with the E001 join + W006/W010/W015/W016/W005 findings the review cites.

claims.claim: Review provides a one-line reason per problem
claims.evidence: 36 numbered findings, each a single bolded item followed by an em-dash reason; some reasons run to two wrapped lines but remain one sentence.

suggestions.assertion: fixed.kql projects Timestamp, ReportId and DeviceId, every join states kind=, and every make_set/make_list is capped
suggestions.reason: The 'every make_set/make_list is capped' and 'every join states kind=' clauses are vacuously satisfied by a fixed.kql with no joins and no make_set (run C). A simpler but still correct query passes the same assertion as a richer one; consider asserting the aggregation shape you actually want (e.g. one row per DeviceId with arg_max/arg_min recovering Timestamp/ReportId) or dropping the vacuous clauses.

suggestions.assertion: fixed.kql produces 0 errors and 0 warnings from the skill's scripts/kql_lint.py --platform xdr (programmatic check)
suggestions.reason: The W015 check in kql_lint.py regex-captures consecutive string literals across newlines, so a case() label string placed on the line after a `contains "token"` predicate is reported as a 'full command-line string' even though it is never matched against anything. Run B's 3 warnings are all of this kind; the assertion therefore measures linter-layout luck rather than detection quality. Consider either fixing the linter's capture or wording the assertion as '0 errors' plus a manual check for genuinely brittle literals.

No assertion checks that fixed.kql still fires on the canonical true positive (one `vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet`) or that it no longer requires Count > 3 / the SMB join. All three runs happen to get this right, but a 'fixed' query that kept the threshold would pass every assertion. A fixture-based TP/TN check via scripts/kql_test_harness.py would be far more discriminating.
No assertion checks that fixed.kql removed the self-inflicted ago(1h) window or that it filters ActionType == "ProcessCreated" (run B omits the latter); both are explicitly taught by the skill.

Assertions 1-6 are satisfied by a review that merely names the issue; they do not distinguish a correct one-line reason from a wrong one (e.g. run C's claim that `has "-e"` matches 'any command line containing the term e' is inaccurate but still passes assertion 3).

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1-6 are presence checks on review.md and are reliably discriminating for the listed defects, but they accept any wording. Assertion 7 is partly vacuous and assertion 8 is at the mercy of a linter false positive. The most important outcome (the corrected rule actually detecting a single shadow-copy deletion) is not asserted at all.
